A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in Escherichiia coli, peptide chain elongation rates in growing cells are constant and maximal in fast-growing bacteria (doublings/h greater than or equal to 1.0), but decreased in slowly-growing bacteria (doubling/h less than 1.0).
the synthesis time of the beta-galactose operon in E. coli is 75s at growth rates above 1 doubling/h and increases linearly to about 90s at growth rates of about 0.5 doubling/h.
the synthesis time is constant in rapidly growing cells, and decreased with the growth rate in slowly growing cells, whereas the peptide-chain growth time is constant in all growing cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis time of the enzyme beta-galacto-sidase in Esch-erichia coli B/R is a function of growth-rate.

the peptide-chain elongation rate in Escherichi coli is maximal at 16 amino acids/s, which is in good agreement with the value of 18 amino acids/s reported for E. coli by others [Brenner, Jacob & Meselson (1961) Nature (London) 190, 576-581].
the synthesis time of a protein is not a constant but a function of growth-rate, and that the synthesis time can be determined experimentally from the kinetics of accumulation of the protein.
